newsitem.title: UK: Aframax tankers firm, Mideast VLCCs dip.
newsitem.headline: Aframax tankers firm, Mideast VLCCs dip.

text.p: The Aframax (80,000 tonne) market was the strongest dirty tanker sector on Tuesday, both in the Mediterranean and in northern Europe, brokers said.
They said cross-Med rates had risen to W115-120 from W110 and inter-U.K./Cont had firmed to W105/110, both about five points up from Monday on good enquiry and a shortage of vessels.
"Owners are holding out for higher rates in the Med...The North Sea very much seems to be on the way up, too," one broker said.
The very large crude carrier (VLCC) sector showed a softer tone in a quiet market, however, amid signs that the market has now peaked from its year high of W75.
"Only a couple of ships have got done today. Unless we get a great rush tomorrow, which looks pretty unlikely, I think rates are set to go down," another broker said.
He said trips from the Middle East to Singapore and the Red Sea had slipped to W72.5 from W75 and voyages to Japan could soon dip too.

West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were steady at W65, with 130,000 barrels vessels (Suezmaxes) unchanged at W87.5/90. Transatlantic VLCCs were fixed at W67.5, some five points up from last week on good enquiry, brokers said.
Caribs/upcoast rates "are floundering on a general lack of activity," a U.S. broker said. "It's the usual summertime blues."
He said 70,000 tonne crude cargoes had fallen to W180 from W200 late last week, while 50,000 tonne crude cargoes had dipped to W190, also from W200.
But current Caribs rates are well above the 1996 average of about W148 and W163 respectively, according to data on the Rigos Chartering Inc Internet site.
European fuel oil was little changed, with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont at W240/245 and cross-Med at W200. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
